cells.tense: Here, with the pen in hand, the fire is already lit and shining on what grows.
cells.act: cut to the logic and act on it
cells.ask: Take this week the next step you already see for something you are growing — no gathering more, no waiting for the whole picture.
cells.core:
You light fires. Where you care for what is growing, your confidence does half the work — the ones you bring along catch the direction before you have explained it — and your patience is real enough that nothing gets forced. When something you planted finally shows what it was becoming, the shine is the point. You let it arrive.

Look at what you are growing right now. One of those things has a next step that is already obvious, and you have been circling it. Take that step this week. Do only what is clear and leave the rest where it is. An enthusiasm that acts on what it actually sees grows sharper than one that keeps circling.
cells.sheetLine: You shine on what you grow, and it grows toward the light.
cells.verb: Lighting fires of enthusiasm and radiating confidence into what they set going.
cells.place: Where care is given to what grows, tending without forcing.

cells.tense: Tomorrow is being lit before the fire that is here has any wood under it.
cells.act: ask the question you do not know the answer to
cells.ask: Ask something you are growing a question whose answer would surprise you, and wait for what it says before you offer your own.
cells.core:
Where you care for what is growing, the bracing has started arriving before the growth does. The next version gets lit while this one is still small — one more thing started, one more direction fanned, one more spark thrown ahead of what is actually here. From your side it is confidence. From what you are tending, nothing gets to finish becoming what it is before it is asked to be something newer.

Ask what you are growing a question whose answer you do not already hold, and wait. You are good at finding the direction. This is about letting the plant or the person tell you where they are going. A fire you keep fanning goes out when nobody feeds what is already burning.

cells.tense: The door was lit once, and you are still standing where it used to be.
cells.act: tend the small thing and learn from it
cells.ask: Choose the smallest living thing you have — a plant, a corner, a person — tend it for a week, and learn what it needs from what it does.
cells.core:
The fire went quiet here. Where you care for what is growing, the carry to bring something along — the shining, the starting, the drawing others after you — is not arriving just now; what is left is maintenance, and the ones around you get tended but not lit from. A door you once stood at has closed behind you, and you are still facing it. What grew under your hands, when it did, grew without force. That is what is being called for again.

Choose the smallest living thing you have — a plant, a corner, a person — tend it for a week, and learn what it needs from what it does rather than from what you remember. Do not push the whole garden. Water what is actually there, and let seven days of it teach you the next step. Shine comes back after something small is thriving under your hands, not before.

cells.tense: The pen that starts fires is writing here, and the name on the page is someone else's.
cells.act: hold the weight as a builder holds stone
cells.ask: Carry one piece fully for someone you tend — no handing it off, no announcement — as work that is yours, not an accident.
cells.core:
You are the one lighting the fires here, and if someone asked, it would sound like luck. You start things for what you are tending, draw people toward a direction, stand behind the growth — and file it all under circumstance. The building holds. The author of the building is not in the story. What you cultivated reached its completion, and the shine on it will not come while the credit sits in someone else's hands.

Carry one piece fully for someone you tend — no handing it off, no announcement — as work that is yours, not an accident. Nobody is asking you to announce it. Put your hands under the weight you keep saying is not yours. The step you lay solidly this week is a piece of a thing that endures.
